title: Don't Drop the Cake
rule: The mayor's cake must never touch the ground.
logline: Benny, twelve and extremely confident, has to carry the mayor's seven-layer birthday cake across Brickton by noon — but the whole town seems determined to slow him down. They are. It's his birthday.
hook_caption: The whole town tried to stop him delivering this cake. There was a reason. 🎂
description: Benny has one job: get the mayor's cake to the town square by noon without it touching the ground. A road closure, forty grocery bags, the slowest parking in history and a park full of sprinklers later… watch it twice. Every obstacle is a clue.

benny.name: Benny
benny.bio: 12. Talks fast, thinks faster (he thinks). Calls himself a professional. Want: deliver the cake by noon. Flaw: so sure of himself he never notices the obvious.

pip.name: Pip
pip.bio: 12. Benny's best friend, on the walkie-talkie. Deadpan. Secretly running the whole operation.

dough.name: Mrs. Dough
dough.bio: The baker. Says 'take the long way' like it's a threat.

plum.name: Officer Plum
plum.bio: Closes roads 'for reasons'. The reasons are big.

grandma.name: Grandma Rose
grandma.bio: Has thirty bags of groceries. Has forty.

lead.name: Bandleader Brass
lead.bio: Leads the Brickton Marching Band. Is practicing. For nothing.

mayor.name: Mayor Bloom
mayor.bio: Wears a sash and a hard hat (he was opening a library). It was never his birthday.

setting_note: Brickton, a sunny pastel brick town: Main Street (bakery at the south end), the alley, the back lane, the park with its sprinklers, and the Town Square with the clock tower, fountain, market stalls and bunting.

premises.premise: A kid must carry the mayor's cake across town by noon; the town keeps stalling him — for his own surprise party.
A town's mayor is accidentally replaced by a goat and nobody notices for a week.
A boy's sneeze is so strong it moves houses; the town wants him for the annual parade.
Every statue in the square swaps places at night; a girl tries to prove it.
A pizza delivery that has to be on time — to a house that keeps moving down the street.
The town clock is five minutes fast and a kid has five minutes to fix it before the wedding.
Two rival bakers bake a cake so big it blocks Main Street.
A kid lies that he can juggle; the whole town shows up to the talent show.
A lost balloon ties the whole town together, literally.
A grandma enters a go-kart race against the mayor.

why: Clear ticking clock (noon) + one simple rule (the cake never touches the ground) + escalating comic obstacles, and a twist that recontextualises every obstacle — so the ending pays off AND the film rewards a second watch.
outline: Deep trailer narrator, ridiculous stakes: the cake must never touch the ground.
Benny, 12, 'a professional'. Mrs. Dough: noon sharp — and take the long way.
Pip on the walkie, deadpan. Clock tower: eleven minutes to noon.
Officer Plum closes the road 'for reasons'. Big ones.
Grandma Rose and her thirty (forty) bags of groceries — stacked on the cake.
Mr. Fig has been parking since Tuesday.
Shortcut through the park. The sprinklers go off. Nope nope nope.
Benny bursts into the square at noon. It's empty.
'Turn around.' SURPRISE! It's his birthday — every obstacle was the town stalling him.
He carried his own birthday cake across town. The cake never touched the ground. It touched his face.
draft:
NARRATOR: In the town of Brickton there is a tradition that the mayor's birthday cake must never touch the ground.
BENNY: That's no problem for me, I'm basically a professional cake delivery person.
NARRATOR: Benny was only twelve years old and was definitely not a professional.
MRS. DOUGH: Please take this cake to the town square by twelve o'clock, and make sure you take the long way.
BENNY: Why would I take the long way when the square is right there?
PIP: Benny, do you have the cake?
BENNY: Yes, I have the cake, Pip.
NARRATOR: On the way, a police officer stopped him and told him the road was closed.
NARRATOR: Then his grandmother asked him to help carry her groceries.
NARRATOR: Then Mr. Fig blocked the lane while parking his car very slowly.
NARRATOR: Benny decided to take a shortcut through the park, but the sprinklers turned on.
NARRATOR: When he finally arrived at the square, there was nobody there.
PIP: Turn around.
EVERYONE: Surprise!
NARRATOR: It was actually Benny's birthday, and the whole town had been delaying him to set up a party.
NARRATOR: Then Benny tripped and fell into the cake.
critique: The hook is a sentence about a tradition. Comedy hook = absurd stakes delivered DEAD serious: give the trailer narrator one line, then cut to the kid.
Benny needs a running bit, not a description: 'I'm a professional' becomes the callback that lands the ending ('Professionally.').
'Take the long way' is the first clue — make it suspicious ('Long. Way.') so a rewatch catches it.
Every obstacle is narrated, not played. Each needs its own two-hander with a punchline: Plum's 'reasons', Grandma's thirty-then-forty bags, Fig 'parking since Tuesday'.
No ticking clock is visible. Cut to the clock tower between obstacles — eleven, eight, three, zero minutes.
Pip is just a voice. Show her — hiding behind a market stall IN THE SQUARE, with people crouched behind her. Viewers won't notice the first time.
The empty square is the all-is-lost beat: let it breathe with a full music drop and the bells.
The twist is explained in one flat line. Instead: rapid callback cuts — Plum, Grandma, Fig — each with a guilty wink and their own line back.
Ending pratfall needs a set-up/payoff: narrator 'the cake never touched the ground' → beat → '…it touched Benny's face.'
Pace: 2:30 of comedy needs fast lines (≤ 10 words), overlaps, and a cut every ~2 s. Voices sped up ~14%.
beat_map: Laugh/reveal every 8–12 s: professional (8s) → 'Long. Way.' (18s) → 'spiritually' (28s) → 'big reasons' (40s) → forty bags (58s) → parking since Tuesday (74s) → sprinklers (88s) → empty square (102s) → SURPRISE (112s) → callbacks (120-132s) → splat (142s).

say: In Brickton, the mayor's birthday cake has one rule.
Three hundred years. Not one crumb on the floor.
Which is fine. Because I'm a professional.
Benny was twelve. He was not a professional.
Town square. Noon sharp. And Benny?
The long way? It's literally right there!
Benny, it's Pip. Do you have the cake?
Do I have the cake. Pip. I am the cake. Spiritually.
Officer, I can explain. It's a cake. It's a legal cake—
Is it a big reason or a—
Around meant the alley. The alley meant Grandma Rose.
Benny, sweetie! Help me with my groceries?
Grandma, I'm holding a seven-layer cake!
Then Mr. Fig tried to park.
Mr. Fig! You've been parking since Tuesday!
It's a car, Mr. Fig! Not a painting!
Benny, the sprinklers go off at—
Nope, nope, nope, nope, nope, nope!
The cake stayed dry. Benny did not.
And then, of course, the marching band.
Cake coming through! Excuse me! Cake!
Benny burst into the town square, and…
Hello? Mayor? Anybody? I have… a cake?
Wrong day? Is it Tuesday? Mr. Fig, is it Tuesday?!
Pip, nobody's here. Is there a second town square?!
The road closure. The groceries. The world's slowest parking.
The whole town had been stalling him for an hour.
I carried my own birthday cake across the entire town?!
And the cake never touched the ground.
